sermon.title: Christians’ Responsibility
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 5:14-16 that Christians are the light of the world and are responsible both to do good works that bring honor to the Father and to speak the word of salvation. He explains that grace and works do not conflict, which “works of the law” we are not saved by, and why quiet Christianity is not enough, ending with Paul’s converting gospel before Felix in Acts 24:25.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he gives some statistics and makes claims about groups, politicians and public issues; these are his own and have not been checked by this site. He reads many verses from memory or paraphrases them (his wording of Ephesians 2:8-9 and of Matthew 19 differs from the NKJV text shown with each section), and where he quotes “I have made you a light for the Gentiles” it is Acts 13:47. “[Unclear]” marks three spots where the captions were not clear (a word near 11:00, a word near 15:10 and a short phrase near 16:00).

chunks.section_question: What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)
chunks.short_answer: He reads Matthew 5:14-16 and asks, “why are Christians hiding out?” He says our responsibility is to let our light shine before men, which means that they “may see your good works.”
chunks.text: Uh, we’re going to be talking about Christians’ responsibility. Matthew 5:14-16: “You are the light of the world,” talking to us, and as they say down south, “A city that is set on the hill cannot be hid.” Why are Christians hiding out? They hide out in their homes, they hide out in the church. They’re worthless. “Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel. A city set on a hill cannot be hid. They put the lamp on a lampstand so it gives light to all that are in the house.” He’s just using a natural illustration; that doesn’t make the book an allegorical book. He’s just given us natural illustrations to understand spiritual things. “Let your light shine before men.” So what is our responsibility? To let our light shine. That is our responsibility. You accept Christ, you accept salvation, you accept eternal life, He puts a responsibility on you to let your light shine before who?

chunks.section_question: Should Christians keep their faith private, or let others see it?
chunks.short_answer: He says people “should see our religion,” and that when men see our good works they “will give honor to your Father in heaven.” He asks, “do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor?”
chunks.text: Men, you see. And He tells us what that shining of the light is: “that they may see your good works.” That’s the shining light. These politicians that say, “I don’t wear my religion on my arm, on my sleeve”: that’s ridiculous. People should see our religion. Right here it says it. Hallelujah. And if you do that, He said those men that you do good works before will give honor to your Father in heaven. Now, do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor? So.

chunks.section_question: Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)
chunks.short_answer: He says “grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other.” We are saved by grace through faith with nothing we can do to earn it, yet we are “created to do” good works, and he says people who “eliminate works” are reading only part of the passage.
chunks.text:
Who’s the light of the world? Those of us who are following Jesus. What does the light of the world do? Good works. And who is to see our good works? Men. Now, grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other. We need to get this clear. There is so much emphasis on grace and faith and no works. I want you to get this in your head, your cranial vacuum; I want to fill it up with some truth right now. All right. “It is by grace that you have been saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves.” Nothing you could do about it. “It is the gift of God.” God freely did it.

“Not by works, so that no man can boast.” I can’t win enough souls to get into heaven. I can’t pray enough hours to get into heaven. I can’t take communion enough to get into heaven, to be saved from my sin. There’s absolutely nothing, for my point, that I can do besides believe the gospel, accept His favor, His death on the cross for my sins. Is that an amen? It’s free. Now, “not of works.” Now, if they would just continue reading, the subject hasn’t stopped yet. He’s still talking about salvation. “We are God’s workmanship.” He’s fashioning us.

See, He’s fashioning us into what? A people that are created, they that in Christ Jesus are what? A new creation. Okay, this grace and faith that brought salvation also is the thing that got us born again, made a new creature. Do you see that? We are a new creature, old things passed away, all things made new. We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do what? But we just read, “not by works,” but we were created to do what? Good works. We have a responsibility to do good works. “Let your light so shine before men that they may see your” what? Good works. And it’s right here in the Scripture, that they eliminate works.

chunks.section_question: Is helping the poor and the sick the main good work of the church?
chunks.short_answer: He says we are saved by grace, not works, but because we are saved “He created us to be people that have our light shining by doing good works.” He says yes, we are supposed to help the poor, but that Jesus’ priority “was to save souls” and the priority of the church is to get the gospel out and “not leave the other undone.”
chunks.text:
And people go to church and they hear the same dumbbell things every Sunday, and they just take, they don’t get into the Word for themselves and ask Jesus to open the Word up to them, and they don’t go at the outside sources to get the Word, and so we just wind up with a bunch of dumbed-down Christians. No, we can’t get saved by the works, but because we’re saved, He created us to be people that have our light shining by doing good works, so people can see the difference and bring honor to the God that we give credit to for the way our life is now. Folks, that’s good stuff. Hallelujah. Good works is not just helping the poor, giving medical attention to people that are sick, giving clothing to the naked. Show me one place in the Bible where Jesus gave any clothing to anyone.

Show, show me one place in the Bible where Jesus gave money to the poor. Show me one place in the Bible where He stopped everything He was doing to go visit all the sick people. I got you thinking. See, if we’d learn how to read this book, we could separate ourselves from these dumb authors of the day that are imprisoning our mind. Yes, we’re supposed to help the poor, the Bible says that, but Jesus never took it out of His priority schedule to do it. His priority was to save souls. Isn’t that right? To bring the gospel to people. That is the priority of the church, to get the gospel out to people who need to get saved, and not leave the other undone. Are you with me?

chunks.section_question: What everyday things does he count as good works?
chunks.short_answer: He lists working and providing for your family, abstaining from sexual activity until married to a person of the opposite sex, and abstaining from alcohol and drugs as good works, and says abstaining from sex outside marriage “places no burden on the community.” He says preachers “need to tell the congregation the truth” even if people leave.
chunks.text:
Working and providing for your family is a good work, folks, scripturally a good work. Work is Bible. You don’t put a burden on your community. Abstaining from sexual activity till married, and married to the opposite sex, not the same sex, places no burden on the community. That’s a good work. And also we avoid sexually transmitted diseases that 50% of Americans have. Abstaining from alcohol and drugs puts no burden on the community for the medical attention, and the legal problems, and the law enforcement to try to take care of the problems, and the job-related downtime. That’s a good work.

Not to have anything to do with alcohol and drugs, is that an amen, church? That’s a good thing. See, these people want to do their things and then they want us to foot the bill to get them out of their problem, and we’re spending billions and billions of dollars correcting these problems after they happen, instead of putting restraints on them to prevent the problem. Christians today are shacking up sexually, cooking up sexually, drugging up; they get high on marijuana and alcohol; they really are up on welfare and not working; they like the tobacco and dying early; divorcing or not marrying at all is the way our society’s going. Okay, and Christians are doing that. Is that a good work? Is divorce a good work? No. Is not getting married a good work and just shacking up? No, it’s not good works. And preachers need to tell the congregation the truth. Can I hear an amen? They may not like it, they may leave. Well, they shouldn’t have been there in the first place if they’re not going to accept Jesus’s gospel and change their life.

chunks.section_question: What “works” does the Bible mean when it says we are not saved by works?
chunks.short_answer: He says the works we are not saved by are the “works of the law,” and he points to Galatians 2:16, Romans 3:28 and Hebrews 10:1. He says these are the shadow laws that “are illustrating what Christ was going to do,” not moral laws like honoring parents or not stealing.
chunks.text:
What are the works that we are not saved by? “Not by works, so that no man can boast.” What are these works that we’re not saved by? Isn’t that a good question? All right. Galatians 2:16: “A man is not justified by the works of the law but by the faith of” who? Jesus Christ. See, so the works we’re not saved by is what? Works of the law. Romans 3:28 says, “A man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” Okay. I go back to the law and I read, I read in the law: “The Lord thy God is one God. Thou shalt have, make no graven images in heaven and earth below, earth, or in the middle of the earth, or whatever, anything in the earth. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain. Thou shalt remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy, and you shall work six days and keep the seventh day a day of rest and a day for God. Thou shalt honor thy mother and thy father. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not commit adultery.

Thou shalt not defraud your neighbor,” greed. “Covet.” “And thou shalt not bear false witness.” So what they’re saying is, I don’t have to keep those laws. I can have an idol, and the Catholic Church has all kinds of them. See, I don’t have to take a day, I don’t have to work six days, and I don’t have to give God any debt, and I can take God’s name and I can live any way I want and bring [unclear] to His name. I can kick my parents out of the house and take the house over. I can go murder, I can go steal Mr. Barnes’s new car. He got, “I’m not under works, brother, I want your car.” Does that make sense to you? See, there’s no sense when you’re throwing out good laws.

So what laws is he talking about? What part of the law are we not saved or justified by? Hebrews 10:1: “The law was a shadow of things to come.” A what? Shadow of things to come. Now, honoring your parents, is that a shadow? No, that’s definite. Not stealing, is that a shadow of things to come? No, that’s definite. That’s a civil law; that’s treating people right; that’s under the law of love your neighbor yourself. Verse 4 of Hebrews 10: “It is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.” So what works of the law is he talking about? The shadow laws that are illustrating what Christ was going to do when He come to really save people. And so yes, the shadow law has been done away with. You see, we can eat shrimp today because it’s a shadow of holiness to come. We live right now, we do good works. Hallelujah. Got it.

chunks.section_question: What good works did Jesus point to for eternal life? (the rich man)
chunks.short_answer: He says the rich man asked what good thing to do to have eternal life, and Jesus answered “keep the commandments.” He says Jesus was quoting the Ten Commandments, which “are civil laws that stay with us,” and that we do not have a right to say we are saved to sin.
chunks.text:
Now, what are good works that obtain eternal life, that give you salvation? There’s good works. So this guy comes, this rich guy comes, and he asks Jesus, “What good thing shall I do?” He didn’t ask what shall I believe in. He says what good thing, because we’re supposed to do what? Good works. What good work shall I do that I may have eternal life, which is knowing Jesus, if you will enter into what? Life. What of the grace and faith thing? He didn’t say that, did he? Did he? “If you want eternal life, you want to possess it, then keep the commandments.” And so the guy is a smart aleck and he says, “Well, which ones? Which commandments? There’s a whole lot of them, you know.” That’s us, you know, we’re always trying to trap the preacher and trap the Bible. “Which one?” And Jesus said, “You shall not murder.” So what’s He quoting? The Ten Commandments, which are civil laws that stay with us. We still work the civil laws. You can’t commit adultery: sexual immorality, including homosexuality, including sex with animals, including orgies, and including incest. This word encompasses it all. You can’t steal, nor bear false witness, lie, blame somebody for something they didn’t do. “Honor your father and your mother.” It doesn’t say if they honor you. It says honor them. “Love your neighbor as yourself.”

Now, He substituted “love your neighbor as yourself” with the covetous law, the last six commandments, and He substituted “love your neighbor,” which is the second commandment. Got it? Now, folks, we got to still do these. These are works that obtain eternal life. These are good works, aren’t they? They didn’t stop. I don’t have a right to say I’m saved to sin, and even Romans said it plainly: “Am I saved to sin?” Then he said, “God forbid.” What? [unclear] Are Christians responsible to do good work too? All right. Isaiah 60:1: “Arise, shine, for your light has come.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? Certainly not! How shall we who died to sin live any longer in it?

chunks.section_question: What does Isaiah 60 say about our light, and what is the “dawn”?
chunks.short_answer: He reads Isaiah 60:1 as present tense: “Arise, shine, for your light has come.” He says the word “dawn” means a gradual light, so a young Christian’s light may be dim, but it is promised to grow “brighter and brighter” until the complete day.
chunks.text: That’s present tense. You got it? Wake up. “Your light [unclear]. What are you looking for? You got it. The glory of the Lord is risen upon you.” His glory is His presence. Okay. “Darkness covers the earth and thick darkness the people.” Number one, your light shines to the peoples. Peoples: different society levels, different races, different colors, different languages. “The Lord will rise upon you and His glory appears over you; nations,” now, we got a whole conglomerate of people in America. You got all races, you got languages, you got different cultures, you got different levels of society and all the rest. That’s a nation. “Nations shall come to your light,” and what’s this one? “Kings,” civil leaders, “to the brightness of your dawn.” Dawn is that gradual light. See, yes, you may not be, as a young Christian, very bright in your light shining, but this word “dawn” is what gives you the understanding that yes, my light’s a little dim, I’m young in God, but I’ve been promised my light will go brighter and brighter and brighter and brighter until the complete day, until I’m completely shining. And that’s important for you to know.

chunks.section_question: What else is light besides good works? (the Word, John 1:1-4)
chunks.short_answer: He says the Word is life, life is the light, and “the spoken word is the light,” as long as you back it up with your lifestyle. He connects John 1:1, John 6:63 and John 1:14 to say that Jesus is the Word, life, truth and light.
chunks.text:
Do civil leaders need to hear or need to see our good works? Yeah. Did hear this gospel of eternal life through faith and grace and keeping His commandments? Yes. And who has the responsibility to hit these civil leaders? We do. We can’t get in our little hurt churches and our little houses and just stay there. Are you with me? Now, what else is light besides good works for peoples, nations, and civil leaders? chunks.section_question: Why did Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles? (Acts 13:46-47)
chunks.short_answer: He says Paul and Barnabas spoke the word of God to the Jews first, and “since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we turn to the Gentiles.” He says people will reject the Word “and still claim they’re going to heaven,” with “no change, no new creation, no born again.” He also says “we need to get studious” and “really learn how to learn.”
chunks.text:
Now, is that clear? See, we need to get studious. We need to really learn how to learn. And we go to church and we just sit there: “When’s he going to get over with? When’s he going to...?” We’re not even paying any attention. We need to learn. “Sanctify them through Thy truth. Thy word is” what? Truth. So the Word is truth, life, life, it’s Jesus, and so forth. Now look at this one, Acts 13:46: Paul and Barnabas answered the Jews boldly, confidently, “All right, we had to speak the word of God to you first.” What did they do with the Word of God? They spoke it. And he had to speak it to you first, because that’s what Jesus told him: “You go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” That’s what Jesus told them. So they obeyed, and the Jews were rejecting it, and so he says, “We have to speak the word of God to you first.” See the light, we gave you the light first.

chunks.section_question: What message will change people’s lives? (the word of salvation)
chunks.short_answer: He says the church has family seminars, financial seminars and divorce-recovery seminars, but “the thing that’s going to save the world is this message of” salvation. He says we can be born again, become new creatures, and be restored when we fall, and “you can’t substitute this with other stuff.”
chunks.text:
Now here He’s saying, “I’ve made you a light,” to speak the Word. What word? “That you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.” What’s the word they’re speaking? The word of salvation. Say it: salvation. You know, in the church we got family seminars, we got financial seminars, we got, you know, divorce recovery seminars, we got all the things. The thing that’s going to save the world is this message of what? Salvation. “The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.” What word spread? The word of salvation. That who spoke? Paul and Barnabas.

The thing that’s going to revolutionize people’s lives is this message of salvation. It’s real. We can be born again, we can become new creatures in Christ Jesus, we can be restored when we fall backward. These things are for us, and it’s in the message of salvation. Hallelujah. You can’t substitute this with other stuff. John 3:19: “This is the verdict.” Now, is there a judgment being made here? That’s a powerful word. Here’s the verdict, I’ve made the decision, this is my judgment: “Light has come into the world, but men love” what? “Darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil.”

And the word of the Lord was being spread throughout all the region.

chunks.section_question: Why do people love darkness and hate the light? (John 3:19-21)
chunks.short_answer: He reads John 3:19, that men love “darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil.” He says people who reject the light “want to be told they’re wrong” in a church that tells them they’re okay, and he urges finding “a teacher of the Word” and getting that Word in you.
chunks.text:
Does that mean we stop preaching that word because people don’t want to hear it? That’s what the American church has done. “Everyone who does evil hates” what? “The light.” See, when you say you’re a Christian and you are committing homosexual sin or sexual sin or stealing, your acts, your behavior tells us you hate the light. How can you say you’re a Christian when this Scripture says if you do these things, you hate the light? You’re a hater. See, when you reject the light, you hate Jesus, you hate the Word, you hate truth. “They will not come to the light.” See, they won’t come to Christianity, they won’t come to Jesus, they won’t come to the Word, for fear that their deeds will be exposed. They want to be told they’re wrong, so they find a church that tells them they’re okay. The blind lead the blind and they all fall into the ditch. Yeah, if you want to go to the ditch, then follow these dumb ministers.

If you want to be delivered, if you want wisdom and understanding, if you want to be a real, committed, true Christian, then find you a teacher of the Word and get that Word in you, and that Word will set you free and deliver you and heal you and do everything that it says it would do, including grow. “But whoever lives by the truth,” see, that’s the good works people, “they come to the light,” see, “and the light exposes, so that it may be seen plainly that what he has done has been done through God.” See, we don’t have a problem with the light because we want to be like the light. Even if we are not there yet, we come in with confidence that He’s going to finish the good work He began in us. So we come to the light, we don’t have a problem being exposed. We want to be exposed, we want to be changed, we want to come to repentance in every area so that we can have a light that shines completely, not just the dawning light. Amen.

chunks.section_question: Do good works save anyone? (what Jesus did in His first thirty years)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus did good works until He was thirty and not one person was saved or healed, so “the good works didn’t save anybody.” Good works bring honor to the Father, he says, but “it’s the spoken word of salvation that brings salvation,” and people need both to see the good works and to hear the Word.
chunks.text:
Yes, so don’t ever feel bad about your dawning light. You got a little light, that’s okay. It’s going to grow, it’s going to keep growing, but you got to be in the Word for it to grow. Now, I’ve said this many a time, and let me tell it to you again. Jesus, who did good works from the time He was born till He was 30 years old, He never sinned, He never disrespected His parents, He worked at a job, never committed adultery, never lied.

And not one person was saved, not one person was healed, not one person hated Him and wanted to kill Him. The good works didn’t save anybody. It brings honor to the Father, but it’s the spoken word of salvation that brings salvation. And Jesus’ first words were what? “Repent, believe the gospel, get baptized for the remission of sin.” That was His message. Now, do we need both light shining in our life? People need to see the good works and bring honor to God who gave us the power to do that. Isn’t that right? But they need to hear the Word if they’re going to get saved.

chunks.short_answer: He says “sitting in our homes” and being a quiet Christian “isn’t going to cut it,” and that this includes not speaking out on political issues, right issues and moral issues. He says Christians are the light of the world by doing good works and by speaking the word of truth, to peoples, nations and kings.
chunks.text: And sitting in our homes and being a nice, quiet Christian isn’t going to cut it. Sitting in America and not speaking out on political issues, right issues, moral issues isn’t going to cut it. Christians are the light of the world by doing good works, and our opponents will give honor to God. Christians are the light of the world by speaking the word of truth, and people will get saved. Christians are the light of the world by speaking the word of truth, by speaking to peoples the word of truth, nations and kings. And Christians, Acts 9:15, the Lord said to Ananias, “Go your way, for Paul is a chosen vessel unto Me to bear My name before” what? “The Gentiles,” the unbeliever, “the kings and the children of Israel.”

chunks.short_answer: He points to Paul before Felix in Acts 24:25: “righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.” He says this is the power of the converting gospel: repent and turn to do right, use self-control, and know there is a judgment coming.
chunks.text:
Acts 26:17: “I’m sending you to open their eyes, turn them from darkness to” what? “Light, and from the power of Satan to the power of God.” You know, the Bible says that He has the power to perform what He promised. Acts 24:25: Paul reasoned of “righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come.” Now, here is the converting gospel, right here. Paul was before Felix, the governor, of the government, and he told Felix, he reasoned, he used logic, he logically presented the truth in an orderly manner. Righteousness, number one: repent from sin, turn to do right. Number two:

Self-control. You got to put some effort into this, you got to put some work into this. And these people that say “not by works,” if you don’t put work into it, you’re not going to conquer it. You got to say no to sin, you got to use self-control to get to church, to learn the Bible, you got to bring some discipline in your life. Can I hear it, amen? This is the power of the converting gospel. Paul’s got it right here, summed up for us. And “the judgment to come”: Felix, if you don’t repent and turn and do right, if you don’t use self-control, you’re going to burn. There’s a judgment coming, and you’re going to burn.

It says Bible morality is the proof that we are Christians.

chunks.section_question: Is Bible morality the proof that we are Christians?
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus said “you will know them by their fruits,” and that Bible morality is the proof that we are Christians. He says speaking it to everyone shows we care and gives people “an opportunity to” convert and change their life.
chunks.text: Didn’t Jesus say, “You will know them by their fruits,” not their faith? You know them by what? Their fruits. You see, how can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit? Jesus said, say, you know the root of the tree by the fruit. And Bible morality is speaking it, and speaking it to everyone shows we care. They’re totally wrong, we’re not hating people by telling them the truth. We care for them, we have a compassion for them, and gives them an opportunity to what? Convert and change their life. How many can raise your hand, say you agree this is the gospel that needs to get out to America? Yes. How many really believe God will back up that gospel with His power and actually convert people?

scriptures.text_nkjv: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles? Even so, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit. A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor can a bad tree bear good fruit. Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Therefore by their fruits you will know them.

faqs.question: What does he say about people who say they don’t wear their religion on their sleeve?
faqs.answer: He calls it “ridiculous” and says “people should see our religion.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

faqs.question: Does he say we can be saved by works?
faqs.answer: No. He says “I can’t win enough souls to get into heaven,” cannot pray or take communion enough, and that there is nothing he can do “besides believe the gospel.” He adds, “It’s free.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.

faqs.question: Why does he say we were created in Christ Jesus?
faqs.answer: He says the same grace and faith that brought salvation made us a new creature, and we were “created to do” good works. He says “we have a responsibility to do good works.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.

faqs.question: What does he say about Jesus and helping the poor?
faqs.answer: He asks readers to show him one place where Jesus gave clothing or money to the poor, or stopped everything to visit all the sick. He says we are supposed to help the poor but “His priority was to save souls.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the shadow laws, like eating shrimp?
faqs.answer: He says the shadow laws were illustrating what Christ would do, and “the shadow law has been done away with.” He says we can eat shrimp today “because it’s a shadow of holiness to come.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with these same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make those who approach perfect.

faqs.question: Does he say the Ten Commandments still apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. He says Jesus’ answer to the rich man quotes the Ten Commandments, which “are civil laws that stay with us,” and that honoring your father and mother and loving your neighbor still apply.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now behold, one came and said to Him, “Good Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?” So He said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good but One, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder,’ ‘You shall not commit adultery,’ ‘You shall not steal,’ ‘You shall not bear false witness,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”

faqs.question: Does he say civil leaders need to hear the gospel?
faqs.answer: Yes. He asks whether civil leaders need to hear or see our good works and answers “yes,” and says “we do” have the responsibility to reach them. He says Christians cannot “get in our little hurt churches and our little houses and just stay there.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Arise, shine; For your light has come! And the glory of the LORD is risen upon you. For behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, And deep darkness the people; But the LORD will arise over you, And His glory will be seen upon you. The Gentiles shall come to your light, And kings to the brightness of your rising.

faqs.question: What does he say the Word is?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus is God, life, the Word and light, so “the Word is light, and the spoken word is what brings light to people.” He quotes the Word becoming flesh, full of grace and truth.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

faqs.question: Should Christians stop preaching because people don’t want to hear it?
faqs.answer: No. He asks, “does that mean we stop preaching that word because people don’t want to hear it?” and says “that’s what the American church has done.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And this is the condemnation, that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For everyone practicing evil hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his deeds should be exposed. But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be clearly seen, that they have been done in God.”

faqs.question: Should I feel bad if my light is only a little light?
faqs.answer: No. He says “don’t ever feel bad about your dawning light,” that it is okay and “it’s going to grow,” but “you got to be in the Word for it to grow.”

faqs.question: What does he say were Jesus’ first words?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus’ first words were “repent, believe the gospel, get baptized for the remission of sin,” and that this was His message.

faqs.question: What does he say is missing in the church?
faqs.answer: He says Felix “shook in fear” and that something missing in the church is people “getting saved from the fear of the Lord,” knowing that if they don’t change their life they’re going to hell.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”

faqs.question: Does he say telling people the truth is hating them?
faqs.answer: No. He says “we’re not hating people by telling them the truth. We care for them, we have a compassion for them,” and it gives them a chance to convert and change their life.
